newsitem.title: UK: Stagecoach shares race ahead on profit surge.
newsitem.headline: Stagecoach shares race ahead on profit surge.

text.p: Stagecoach Plc, the transport group which has seen explosive growth in the last year, reported a 127 percent surge in half year profits on Thursday, sending its shares racing ahead.

Pretax profits for the half year to October 12 hit a record 47 million pounds ($78.91 million), with the dividend raised by 43 percent to three pence. The payout reflected the group's 15 million pounds profit from the sale of its 21.7 percent stake in Strathclyde Buses. Stagecoach shares were up 29 pence at 612-1/2 on the news.
Brian Souter, chairman of the group said the results were excellent and highlighted its development into a diversified transport oeprator embracing rail as well as buses.
The results are the first since the group's high profile acquisitions of the British rail rolling stock company Porterbrook and the Swedish bus group Swebus.

"The integration of Porterbrook and Swebus is proceeding and I am confident of a successful outcome," said Souter. The results breakdown showed UK bus operating margins up to 15.6 percent from 14.8 percent and passenger volumes up 1.5 percent.

South West Trains passenger income was 128 million, with profit of 1.3 million before restructuring costs. It saw a seven percent hike in passenger journeys. Porterbrook profits for the six weeks since acquisition was 13.5 million, ahead of expectations. The overseas bus unit was mixed, with a positive European growth outlook marred by problems in African bus operations. ($1=.5956 Pound)
